title: Sparse Output Prefetch + Resumable Toollets SDK Manifest (PRD WIP)
content:
PURPOSE:
This is a lightweight PRD/manifest describing an experiment-grade feature set for Hosted API: a) sparse (bandwidth-lean) progressive output format, b) proactive prefetch + cursored resume semantics for long-running sessions, and c) a micro-transaction model for tool calls ("toollets") that lets clients commit or rollback partial results without blocking the main stream. The goal is to provide SDK ergonomics for low-latency clients (mobile/edge) while preserving server-side batching and caching economics.

PRIORITY PROBLEM STATEMENT:
Many customers want the UX of progressive model output (partial answers) but run over constrained networks (mobile, satellite), and/or need to call external tools (search, DB, code execution) mid-stream. Current streaming semantics are either heavy (full transcripts) or synchronous (blocking tool calls). This leads to: high bandwidth usage, poor resiliency on flaky networks, spiky latency when tool calls block, and poor developer ergonomics for resume/retry.

SUCCESS METRICS (30/60/90):
- 30d: SDK prototype integrated in 3 client apps; measured 30% reduction in median bytes/response for target prompts.
- 60d: Live canary traffic shows 10% reduction in per-token cost due to increased cache hits (prefix prefetching).
- 90d: <1% unhandled session loss after network interruption across canary cohort; toollet commit success >= 99.5%.

GOALS:
- Provide a compact frame format that transmits only deltas (sparse patches) and minimal annotations to reconstruct a coherent partial response on the client.
- Add a cursor/resume token so clients can reconnect to a session and request missing ranges instead of re-running full prompts.
- Define a tiny transactional model for tool calls (toollets) with commit/abort frames to permit speculative, optimistically-executed external calls without stalling the main stream.
- SDK ergonomics: easy-to-use client APIs that expose progressive content, tool-call lifecycle, and automatic prefetch heuristics.

NON-GOALS:
- Not supporting multi-party session replication in this phase.
- Not implementing full deterministic replay guarantees for all tool interactions.

USER STORIES / EXAMPLES:
1) Mobile note-taking app: user starts a long summary; client receives progressive skeleton text (headlines) first and incrementally fills content. On weak network, app reconnects and requests missing frames; user sees coherent partial content quickly.
2) Customer support agent: system streams an answer and speculatively calls a CRM lookup toollet; if toollet commit fails, the UI shows a secondary suggestion and continues generating.
3) Embedded widget: low-bandwidth clients only subscribe to headline frames to save bytes and request detail frames on tap.

PRINCIPLES / DESIGN CONSTRAINTS:
- Minimal wire footprint for common-case mobile usage.
- Backwards-compatible: fall back to current streaming if client doesn't support new frames.
- Server batching and caching must remain effective; frames should be coalescible into GPU batches.
- Simple SDK API that avoids exposing low-level frame plumbing to most apps.

PROPOSED PROTOCOL (high level):
- Session Start: POST /v1/sessions -> returns session_id, initial_resume_token, supported_capabilities.
- Stream frames: chunked transfer over HTTP/2 SSE or websocket. Each frame is typed: {frame_id, token_range_start, token_range_end, frame_type, payload}
  - frame_type examples: HEADLINE, DELTA, CHECKPOINT, TOOLLET_OP (speculative), TOOLLET_COMMIT, TOOLLET_ABORT, RESUME_HINT
- Resume model: client reconnects with resume_token and requests missing token ranges or asks server to stream onward from last_ack.
- Prefetch hint: clients can send a small telemetry-driven hint: desired_fidelity: [HEADLINE|SUMMARY|FULL] to control server bandwidth/latency tradeoffs.

NOTE: above is an abstracted view — below we give two concrete payload sketches (plain text):

CONCRETE FRAME SKETCHES (PLAIN TEXT EXAMPLES):
- HEADLINE frame:
  frame_id: f_001
  frame_type: HEADLINE
  token_range: 0-12
  payload: "Q3 product launch: summary bullets"

- DELTA frame (sparse patch):
  frame_id: f_002
  frame_type: DELTA
  token_range: 12-84
  payload: "Added: 'We will prioritize latency...'. Removed: 'old sentence'"

- TOOLLET_OP (speculative call):
  frame_id: t_100
  frame_type: TOOLLET_OP
  op_id: op-99
  tool: crm-lookup
  args: "{email: 'user@acme.com'}"
  payload: "Speculative note: found 2 matches"

- TOOLLET_COMMIT:
  frame_id: t_100-c
  frame_type: TOOLLET_COMMIT
  op_id: op-99
  result_ref: res-8812
  payload: "Customer record id: 8812"

SDK SURFACE (developer friendly):
- Languages: JS, Kotlin, Swift prototypes.
- Primary primitives (pseudo API):
  - Session.create(prompt, opts) -> Session object
  - Session.on('partial', (fragment) => {}) // HEADLINE/DELTA events
  - Session.callTool(name, args, {speculative: true}) -> ToolHandle
  - ToolHandle.on('commit', (resultRef) => {}), ToolHandle.on('abort', () => {})
  - Session.resume(resumeToken, {fromToken: 20}) -> continues stream from token 20
  - Session.requestFidelity(level) -> HEADLINE|SUMMARY|FULL

ERGONOMICS GUIDELINES:
- Default SDK behavior: subscribe to HEADLINE + DELTA. SDK auto-applies DELTAs to client buffer and exposes a stable 'currentText' property.
- Provide a 'sparse-mode' where only HEADLINE frames are fetched until client explicitly requests more detail (tap-to-expand pattern).
- Tool calls are represented as non-blocking futures. By default they are speculative; SDK surfaces commit/abort and lets developer choose how to render fallback content.
- Provide a small local cache of resume tokens and frames (LRU, configurable size) to accelerate reconnects.

OPERATIONAL / OBSERVABILITY CONSIDERATIONS:
- Telemetry: track bytes/frame, frames-per-session, toollet_commit_rate, average time-to-commit, resume_success_rate.
- Quotas: toollet invocations counted separately from generation tokens. Introduce a small fixed charge for speculative toollets to discourage wasteful speculative traffic.
- Rollout: feature gated by capability flags in session response (clients should check supported_capabilities).

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES (server-side):
- Frames can be produced from a single model pass by materializing lightweight checkpoints at token boundaries and computing diffs for DELTA frames.
- Speculative toollets: executed in an isolated worker pool; their results are stored as result refs and optionally replayed into the main generator if committed.
- Resume token: opaque string encoding session id + last_checkpoint_seq + signing nonce; stored in session store with TTL (configurable).

RISKS & MITIGATIONS:
- Risk: fragmentation leads to inconsistent client state if frames drop. Mitigation: include frame_seq numbers and a periodic CHECKPOINT frame that contains canonical snapshot for recovery.
- Risk: speculative toollets create cost overhead. Mitigation: default speculative=false for high-paying plans, and introduce per-op throttle.
- Risk: developer confusion with too many modes. Mitigation: SDK defaults (HEADLINE+auto DELTA apply) and a simple migration guide plus playground.

ROLLOUT PLAN / EXPERIMENTS:
- Phase 1 (internal): JS SDK + server canary for 5% internal traffic. Collect bytes/session and resume success.
- Phase 2 (developer early access): opt-in customers; provide telemetry dashboard and billing telemetry for toollet ops.
- Phase 3 (general availability): enable as opt-out for mobile clients; refine billing.

OPEN QUESTIONS (needs decisions):
- How large should resume token TTL be by default (1h vs 24h)?
- Default speculative tool policy per plan — free vs paid vs enterprise.
- Should result refs be user-accessible IDs for offline reconciliation? Privacy/PII implications.

ACTIONS / TODOs:
- [ ] Prototype JS SDK: apply DELTA patching and resume token handling (owner: Miguel).
- [ ] Server-side: implement checkpoint + diff generator (owner: Applied ML team, Rohit).
- [ ] Billing: propose pricing delta primitives for speculative toollets (owner: GTM finance, Aisha).
- [ ] Security review for tool result refs (owner: Security, Hannah).
- [ ] Draft developer migration guide and quickstart sample app (owner: DevX).

NOTES TO REVIEWERS:
This is intentionally a compact tradeoff doc; the primary aim is to validate that the SDK ergonomics reduce bandwidth by focusing on sparse frames and to ensure toollet lifecycle fits naturally into streaming without introducing blocking latencies. Please annotate the linked Confluence doc with concrete telemetry KPIs you want to see in the canary.

END
